items.title: Hook-shaped Schur expansions are equivalent to uniformity of the descent-set distribution
items.author: Avichai Marmor
items.work: Schur-positivity of short chords in matchings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled proposition `prop:hook schur positive` at source lines 1334-1341: a set A has a hook-shaped non-negative Schur expansion if and only if the number |A(D = J)| depends only on |J|, with c_k the count on [k]. The author's proof (source lines 1343-1352) has two directions of different character. The forward direction is a bijective computation: it uses that a hook tableau of shape (N-k,1^k) has exactly k descents and that each k-subset arises from exactly one hook tableau (line 1344), which turns the uniform hypothesis into the displayed generating-function identity (lines 1345-1348) before the Schur-positivity criterion is applied (line 1349). The converse is not a computation at all: it rests on the uniqueness of the descent-set distribution of a generating function, cited from Adin and Roichman at line 1351. The statement is a two-way equivalence whose two halves are proved by completely different means.
